security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, if a future Zimt (memory tagging) implementation or bhyve VMM writes a non-zero value to bit 36 of any __x__envcfg CSR (menvcfg/senvcfg/henvcfg/uenvcfg) or mseccfg, thinking it enables asynchronous store-tag-check reporting, this bit is now WPRI per the updated spec. Setting WPRI bits to non-zero values risks unpredictable behavior on current hardware and functional misbehavior on future hardware that repurposes bit 36. In particular, bhyve's hypcsr struct already saves/restores senvcfg (riscv.h:67) without any WPRI-bit masking, so a malicious or buggy guest OS could set bit 36 in senvcfg, and bhyve would blindly restore it, causing the host to write a non-zero WPRI bit into the physical CSR.
security_spec.summary: PR #80 removes MT_ASYNC (bit 36) from all envcfg CSRs and mseccfg; FreeBSD's bhyve already saves/restores senvcfg without WPRI-bit masking, so any future Zimt code that writes bit 36 violates the new spec and risks undefined behavior on WPRI-bit writes
